metadata.title: Comparison of PIAAC and PISA Frameworks for Numeracy and Mathematical Literacy

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD working paper is a framework-comparison document rather than an empirical analysis of microdata. It describes that both PISA and PIAAC use large nationally representative samples selected via stratified random sampling, with minimum completed respondent targets (PISA: at least 4,500 completed respondents from at least 150 schools; PIAAC: at least 5,000 completed respondents aged 16–65). The paper explains that PISA and PIAAC results are scaled using IRT-based continuous proficiency scales and reported in proficiency levels/bands, but it does not specify any student or replicate weight variables for re-analysis in this paper. For analysts using PISA/PIAAC microdata, the appropriate complex survey design weights and replicate weights should be applied as specified in the respective PISA/PIAAC technical documentation; this paper itself does not conduct weighted estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This paper does not estimate student-level predictive models or report PV-based achievement outcomes; it provides a conceptual and methodological comparison of the PIAAC numeracy and PISA mathematical literacy frameworks. Because there is no analysis of cognitive achievement scores with PVs in this working paper, PV handling and missing-data handling strategies are not applicable to the paper’s own results. Any PV and missing-data procedures would instead be handled within the official PISA/PIAAC technical volumes, which are referenced but not re-implemented here.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic microdata sample is constructed in this paper. The document compares framework and methodology features of PISA (including cycles 2000–2012, with emphasis on PISA 2012) and PIAAC (including the first wave and general design), describing sampling targets and assessment design constraints rather than analyzing a specific dataset extract.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education Working Paper compares how PIAAC numeracy and PISA mathematical literacy are conceptualized and operationalized, focusing on assessment design choices that shape interpretation of proficiency results. It describes that both programs use nationally representative stratified random sampling, but differ in testing context (PISA: group testing of 15-year-olds in schools; PIAAC: individual household testing of adults aged 16–65) and in time constraints that affect item counts and item types. The paper explains that both assessments use IRT-based scaling to produce continuous proficiency scales and report proficiency levels/bands, while also highlighting differences in scale ranges, response probabilities, and the number of reporting levels (5 in PIAAC vs 6 in PISA). It further details differences in item formats, response/action classifications, and complexity schemes, including how PIAAC’s adaptive computer-based routing and automatic scoring constrain open constructed responses. Overall, it concludes that direct comparisons of reported proficiency levels across PISA and PIAAC require caution because the underlying measurement criteria and item difficulty distributions are not equivalent.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical framework-comparison working paper. It does not conduct an original student-level analysis, does not train or evaluate machine learning models, and does not report PV-based predictive performance metrics; therefore fields such as total_students, country-level sample sizes, PV handling, missing-data handling, and main findings are not populated. The paper’s contribution is methodological: it synthesizes and contrasts PISA/PIAAC constructs, assessment methodologies, item/task characteristics, and comparability considerations for policy interpretation.
